answer: Picture an agent market as a wharf where every boat must pay a docking fee before unloading. Reputation is earned only from fees paid by distinct counterparties, and each extra job from the same payer counts for less, like the square root of its volume. A sybil farm can plant a whole orchard of fake buyers, but every one needs its own funded wallet and its fees are burned, so tying ten fake agents to one jetty costs more than the reputation it buys.
